results.note: ingest/backfill.py run_backfill takes indicator_key, where None means all keys, and calls recipes[entry.backfill_recipe]. The named test proves a single key reaches only its own recipe. test_backfill_entry_point_can_run_all_registered_backfillable_keys proves the all-keys mode and that not_backfillable entries are skipped. Both tests run in the offline suite.

The only test that runs the real persist_board -> persist_datapoint path with origin='backfill' against the real unique index is marked @pytest.mark.integration. pyproject.toml:33 sets addopts '-m not integration', so the gate deselected it (358 passed, 66 deselected); it never ran. The offline test test_backfill_writes_through_persist_board_with_backfill_origin swaps persist_board for a fake, so it only proves a function with that name was called with origin='backfill'. This is the same misclassification the owner flagged in US-902: tests/test_persist_board.py uses an unmarked postgres fixture, and integration is reserved for live third-party endpoints (pyproject.toml:27).

Attempt 2 did replace the circular fake-dedup test with a real Postgres rerun test, but it marked that test @pytest.mark.integration. The test touches no live third-party endpoint, only a throwaway schema, yet the marker means the default `uv run pytest -q` gate deselects it. So no executed test proves that rerunning a backfill leaves no duplicate rows. It is the same gap that failed US-902 attempts 1-2.

assert_backfill_coverage in ingest/registry.py raises an AssertionError naming the entry when it has neither backfill_recipe nor not_backfillable. The test asserts the message matches 'silent_indicator'. A companion test covers an entry that names an unknown recipe. run_backfill runs the same check before any write.

The test loads the real registry.yaml. It asserts that sol_active_addresses (Helius getBlock reason) and sol_staking (Validators.app reason) both declare not_backfillable with different reasons. It then asserts the coverage check passes on the full registry against BACKFILL_RECIPES. The test runs offline.
The US-903-C6 gate `uv run pytest -q` exited 0 (358 passed, 66 deselected).

note: Not faked, but the only direct proof of the shared write path and idempotency (a real-Postgres rerun test) is wrongly marked @pytest.mark.integration, so the gate deselects it and it never runs. This is the same marker misclassification that failed US-902; removing the marker, as test_persist_board.py does, would likely close C2 and C3. Every backfillable entry points at a placeholder 'noop' recipe, which the story notes explicitly allow.
